cves.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an Expression Language Statement (Expression Language Injection)
cves.description: Apache Log4j2 2.0-beta9 through 2.15.0 (excluding security releases 2.12.2, 2.12.3, and 2.3.1) JNDI features used in configuration, log messages, and parameters do not protect against attacker-controlled LDAP and other JNDI-related endpoints. An attacker who can control log messages or log message parameters can execute arbitrary code loaded from LDAP servers when message lookup substitution is enabled.
cves.fix_summary: Upgrade log4j-core to 2.17.1 or later. As an interim mitigation, set log4j2.formatMsgNoLookups=true or remove the JndiLookup class from the classpath. The vulnerable JNDI message-lookup functionality was disabled by default in 2.15.0 and completely removed in 2.16.0.
cves.fixed_version: Log4j 2.17.1 (2.15.0 disabled JNDI lookups by default; 2.16.0 removed them entirely)
cves.name: Log4Shell
cves.poc_note: Public proof-of-concept code was published within hours of disclosure; widely documented.
cves.title: Apache Log4j2 JNDI Remote Code Execution (Log4Shell)

cves.description: The (1) TLS and (2) DTLS implementations in OpenSSL 1.0.1 before 1.0.1g do not properly handle Heartbeat Extension packets, which allows remote attackers to obtain sensitive information from process memory via crafted packets that trigger a buffer over-read.
cves.fix_summary: Upgrade to OpenSSL 1.0.1g or later. After patching, revoke and reissue any TLS certificates and private keys that may have been exposed in process memory, and force password resets for affected services.
cves.name: Heartbleed
cves.poc_note: Public PoC published at disclosure; memory contents (including private keys) demonstrably recoverable.
cves.title: OpenSSL TLS Heartbeat Extension Information Disclosure (Heartbleed)

cves.affected_versions: Windows Vista SP2 through Windows 10 1607 / Windows Server 2016 with SMBv1 enabled
cves.cwe_name: Improper Restriction of Operations within the Bounds of a Memory Buffer
cves.description: The SMBv1 server in Microsoft Windows Vista SP2, Windows Server 2008 SP2 and R2 SP1, Windows 7 SP1, Windows 8.1, Windows Server 2012 Gold and R2, Windows RT 8.1, and Windows 10 Gold, 1511, and 1607, and Windows Server 2016 allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code via crafted packets, aka Windows SMB Remote Code Execution Vulnerability. Basis of the WannaCry ransomware worm.
cves.fix_summary: Apply the MS17-010 security update. Disable SMBv1 (it is disabled by default in Windows 10 1709 and later / Windows Server 2019) and block TCP port 445 at the network perimeter.
cves.name: EternalBlue
cves.poc_note: Public exploit code widely available; used by the WannaCry worm (May 2017) and later by NotPetya.
cves.score_note: NVD's CVSS 3.x vector for this CVE carries AC:H; the 8.1 score is reproduced exactly by the FIRST formula from this vector. The vector was originally published as CVSS 3.0; the 3.0 and 3.1 base-score formulas are identical.
cves.title: Microsoft Windows SMBv1 Remote Code Execution (EternalBlue)

cves.affected_versions: Windows Print Spooler on all supported Windows versions (July 2021)
cves.description: A remote code execution vulnerability exists when the Windows Print Spooler service improperly performs privileged file operations. An attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability could run arbitrary code with SYSTEM privileges.
cves.fix_summary: Apply the July 6, 2021 (or later) security updates. Apply KB5005010 guidance: restrict installation of new printer drivers (Point and Print restrictions) and ensure NoWarningNoElevationOnInstall / UpdatePromptSettings are 0 or absent. Consider disabling the Print Spooler service where printing is not needed.
cves.fixed_version: July 6, 2021 out-of-band security updates (e.g. KB5004945); see also KB5005010
cves.name: PrintNightmare
cves.poc_note: Accidental public disclosure of PoC by researchers in June 2021; widely reproduced.
cves.score_note: PR:L (low privileges required) is what separates this 8.8 from the 9.8 of a fully unauthenticated RCE with the same impact metrics.
cves.title: Windows Print Spooler Remote Code Execution (PrintNightmare)

cves.affected_versions: Spring Framework 5.3.0-5.3.17, 5.2.0-5.2.19, and older unsupported versions (JDK 9+, Tomcat WAR deployment)
cves.description: A Spring MVC or Spring WebFlux application running on JDK 9+ may be vulnerable to remote code execution via data binding. The specific exploit requires the application to run on Tomcat as a WAR deployment. If the application is deployed as a Spring Boot executable jar (the default), it is not vulnerable to the exploit; however, the nature of the vulnerability is more general and there may be other ways to exploit it.
cves.fix_summary: Upgrade to Spring Framework 5.3.18 or 5.2.20 (or later). The fix disallows the classloader manipulation pattern used by the exploit. Applications deployed as executable jars were not directly exploitable but should still upgrade.
cves.name: Spring4Shell
cves.poc_note: Public PoC published within days of disclosure; exploitation observed in the wild.
cves.title: Spring Framework Remote Code Execution (Spring4Shell)

cves.affected_versions: HTTP/2 server implementations prior to patched releases (e.g. nghttp2 < 1.57.0, Go < 1.21.3 / 1.20.10, Apache httpd < 2.4.58)
cves.description: The HTTP/2 protocol allows a denial of service (server resource consumption) because request cancellation can reset many streams quickly, as exploited in the wild in August through October 2023.
cves.fix_summary: Upgrade HTTP/2 server libraries and servers to patched releases. Apply RST_STREAM rate limiting and connection-level stream accounting as defense in depth; the underlying protocol behavior is mitigated by implementations limiting how quickly streams can be opened and reset.
cves.fixed_version: Vendor patches (nghttp2 1.57.0, Go 1.21.3/1.20.10, Apache httpd 2.4.58, nginx 1.25.3)
cves.name: HTTP/2 Rapid Reset
cves.poc_note: Attack technique publicly described by Google, Cloudflare and AWS at disclosure; used in record-breaking DDoS attacks Aug-Oct 2023.
cves.product: HTTP/2 protocol implementations (nghttp2, Go, Apache httpd, nginx, etc.)
cves.title: HTTP/2 Rapid Reset Denial of Service

cves.affected_versions: XZ Utils 5.6.0 and 5.6.1 (upstream tarballs only; the Git repository was not affected)
cves.description: Malicious code was discovered in the upstream tarballs of xz, starting with version 5.6.0. Through a series of complex obfuscations, the liblzma build process extracts a prebuilt object file from a disguised test file, which is then used to modify specific functions in the liblzma code. This results in a modified liblzma library that can be used by any software linked against this library, intercepting and modifying the data interaction with this library.
cves.fix_summary: Downgrade to an uncompromised version such as XZ Utils 5.4.6, or upgrade to the clean upstream 5.6.2 release. Any host that ran 5.6.0/5.6.1 with SSH exposed should be treated as possibly compromised: hunt for malicious activity and rebuild from a known-good image where warranted. The backdoor never reached stable releases of major distributions.
cves.fixed_version: Downgrade to 5.4.6 (CISA recommendation); clean upstream release 5.6.2 (29 May 2024)
cves.name: xz backdoor
cves.poc_note: The backdoored release tarballs themselves were public; no separate PoC is needed. Caught before exploitation at scale, which is why it is NOT in CISA KEV.
cves.title: XZ Utils Supply-Chain Backdoor (liblzma)

cves.description: Microsoft Exchange Server Remote Code Execution Vulnerability. This vulnerability is part of an attack chain. The initial attack requires the ability to make an untrusted connection to Exchange server port 443. This can be achieved by an attacker who can connect to the Exchange server.
cves.fix_summary: Apply the March 2, 2021 out-of-band Exchange security updates immediately. Microsoft also published a one-click mitigation tool and guidance to check for webshells and indicators of compromise, since the flaw was exploited in the wild (HAFNIUM) before patching.
cves.fixed_version: March 2, 2021 out-of-band Exchange security updates (cumulative update patches)
cves.name: ProxyLogon
cves.poc_note: Public PoC published within days; mass exploitation by multiple threat actors observed March 2021.
cves.score_note: Microsoft's own CNA score for this CVE is 9.1 (no availability impact in their assessment); the NVD score of 9.8 is used here, as for all entries in this dataset.
cves.title: Microsoft Exchange Server Remote Code Execution (ProxyLogon)

cves.affected_versions: Windows Server 2008 R2 through Windows Server 2019 domain controllers (Netlogon)
cves.cwe_name: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm
cves.description: An elevation of privilege vulnerability exists when an attacker establishes a vulnerable Netlogon secure channel connection to a domain controller, using the Netlogon Remote Protocol (MS-NRPC). An attacker who successfully exploited the vulnerability could run a specially crafted application on a device on the network.
cves.fix_summary: Apply the August 2020 security update and move Netlogon to enforcement mode (secure RPC required), which Microsoft made the default in the February 2021 update. Verify no legacy devices still rely on vulnerable Netlogon secure channels.
cves.fixed_version: August 2020 security update; secure RPC enforcement mode February 2021
cves.name: Zerologon
cves.poc_note: Public PoC (Secura whitepaper + tools) published September 2020; exploitation observed in the wild within weeks.
cves.score_note: Microsoft's own CNA score for this CVE is 5.5 (local attack vector, low privileges in their assessment); the NVD score of 10.0 is used here, as for all entries in this dataset. The discrepancy is documented here precisely because CVSS involves analyst judgment — the vector string must always accompany the score.
cves.title: Netlogon Elevation of Privilege (Zerologon)

cves.affected_versions: Windows 7 SP1, Windows Server 2008 R2 SP1, Windows Server 2008 SP2, Windows XP / Server 2003 (out of support, patched exceptionally)
cves.description: A remote code execution vulnerability exists in Remote Desktop Services formerly known as Terminal Services when an unauthenticated attacker connects to the target system using RDP and sends specially crafted requests. This vulnerability is pre-authentication and requires no user interaction. An attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability could execute arbitrary code on the target system.
cves.fix_summary: Apply the May 2019 security updates (Microsoft also patched out-of-support Windows XP/2003). Disable RDP where not needed, require Network Level Authentication (NLA), and never expose RDP directly to the internet.
cves.fixed_version: May 14, 2019 security updates (e.g. KB4499175 for Windows 7 / Server 2008 R2)
cves.name: BlueKeep
cves.poc_note: Public PoC and Metasploit module published; wormable by design (pre-auth, no user interaction). No self-propagating worm was observed at scale, but exploitation was confirmed.
cves.title: Remote Desktop Services Remote Code Execution (BlueKeep)

dataset.name: swarm-triage-cve-dataset
dataset.scope: Only already-fixed, publicly disclosed CVEs. No live exploitation, no scanning, no unpublished data. All scores and vectors are the NVD (NIST) CVSS 3.x base scores as published on nvd.nist.gov; where the vendor CNA score differs, it is noted in score_note.
dataset.verification_note: Every CVSS vector and score in this file was cross-checked against NVD and at least one independent public source on 2026-11-17. The pipeline recomputes each base score from its vector (FIRST formula) and fails validation if it does not match the stored score.
